objective: Establish and verify the reproducible production application foundation for SkillForge.
implementation: Created a production Next.js App Router application with strict TypeScript, validated environment configuration, deterministic scripts, and a locked dependency graph.
Defined eleven framework-independent domain boundaries and enforced their independence from Next.js, React, UI, and provider implementations.
Added a mobile-first SkillForge product shell plus loading, error, global-error, not-found, unauthorized, and forbidden experiences.
Added unit and component tests, a clean-install verification workflow, GitHub Actions quality gate, architecture documentation, and a CI formatting-scope repair.

evidence: Prettier, ESLint with zero warnings, Next route type generation, and strict TypeScript all passed locally and in GitHub Actions.

verification.name: HTTP smoke
evidence: The home, forbidden, and unauthorized routes returned HTTP 200; an unknown route returned HTTP 404; expected homepage content was present; no application server errors were observed.
The shell presents the teacher-controlled class lifecycle as the central product workflow.
The first screen explains what SkillForge is, what evidence it uses, and the next class-lifecycle steps without requiring menu discovery.
The implementation preserves the locked Learning Operating System identity, multi-role scope, and teacher-authority principle.
Reproducible scripts, CI, an ADR, strict boundaries, exact dependencies, and a clean-install proof are present.
Loading, recoverable error, global error, not-found, sign-in-required, and access-restricted experiences are implemented.
Static proxy review verified landmarks, labeled sections, focus-visible treatment, reduced-motion support, semantic links and buttons, and ordinary navigable auth fallback routes.

decisions: Use one Next.js App Router deployable organized as a modular monolith.
Keep domain entry points independent from frameworks, UI, and provider implementations, with both lint and test enforcement.
Use ordinary unauthorized and forbidden routes until authentication is implemented instead of depending on experimental authorization interrupts.
Treat LoopForge protocol records and generated charter documents as outside Prettier ownership while continuing to format application documentation.
problems: BLOCKER-014 remains open: Vercel preview deployments for PR #16 failed, but the connected Vercel API and unauthenticated browser cannot access the existing project or its logs.
A browser screenshot and runtime accessibility audit could not be captured in the sandbox; visual production verification remains pending under SUCCESS-009 and TASK-009.
